   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> Basis of Presentation</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Overview</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The accompanying unaudited interim Consolidated Financial Statements of H.B. Fuller Company and Subsidiaries have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles for interim financial information and the instructions to Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q and Article <em style="font: inherit;">10</em> of Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X.</em> Accordingly, they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all of the information necessary for a fair presentation of results of operations, comprehensive income, financial position&#160;and cash flows in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles. In our opinion, the unaudited interim Consolidated Financial Statements reflect all adjustments of a normal recurring nature considered necessary for the fair presentation of the results for the periods presented. Operating results for interim periods are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of results that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be expected for the fiscal year as a whole.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues, expenses and related disclosures at the date of the financial statements and during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from these estimates. These unaudited interim Consolidated Financial Statements should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and Notes thereto included in our Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for the year ended&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em> as filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-11-30_2026-02-28" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142496628" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>New Accounting Pronouncements</i></p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024,&#160;</em>the FASB&#160;issued Accounting Standards Update ("ASU")&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">No.</em></i>&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em></i>-<i><em style="font: inherit;">03,</em></i>&#160;<i>Income Statement - Reporting Comprehensive Income - Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic</i>&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">220</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">40</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</i>, which requires additional disclosure of the nature of expenses included in our Consolidated Financial Statements. Our effective date of this ASU is our fiscal year ending&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 2, 2028.&#160;</em>We are currently evaluating the impact of adopting this guidance on the related financial statement disclosures.&#160;</p> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023,&#160;</em>the FASB issued ASU&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">No.</em></i>&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">2023</em></i>-<i><em style="font: inherit;">09,</em></i>&#160;<i>Income Taxes (Topic</i>&#160;<i><em style="font: inherit;">740</em>): Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures</i>. This ASU requires entities to provide additional information in the rate reconciliation and additional disclosures about income taxes paid. This guidance requires public entities to disclose in their rate reconciliation table additional categories of information about federal, state, and foreign income taxes and to provide more details about the reconciling items in some categories if the items meet a quantitative threshold. Our effective date of this ASU is our fiscal year ending&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> November 28, 2026.&#160;</em>We are currently evaluating the impact of adopting this guidance on the related financial statement disclosures.&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Recently issued accounting standards or pronouncements <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> disclosed above have been excluded as they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> relevant to the company.</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p>
   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-11-30_2026-02-28" name="ful:SupplierFinanceProgramPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c142496629" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Supplier Finance Program</i></p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We have agreements with <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties to provide supplier finance programs which facilitate participating suppliers' ability to finance payment obligations of the Company with designated <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party financial institutions. Participating suppliers <em style="font: inherit;"> may, </em>at their sole&#160;discretion, elect to finance <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> or more payment obligations of the Company prior to their scheduled due dates at a discounted price to participating financial institutions. The Company has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> economic interest in the sale of these suppliers&#8217; receivables and <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> direct&#160;financial relationship with the financial institutions concerning these services. The Company&#8217;s obligations to its suppliers, including amounts due and scheduled payment dates, are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> impacted by suppliers&#8217; decisions to finance amounts under these arrangements. The outstanding payment obligations that were confirmed as valid and remained outstanding as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em><span style="color:#000000;">, and </span><em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em><span style="color:#000000;">, were</span>&#160;approxi<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">mately&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142492864" contextRef="i_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SupplierFinanceProgramObligation" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">8,633</ix:nonFraction> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142492865" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:SupplierFinanceProgramObligation" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">7,379</ix:nonFraction>, respectively.</span> These obligations under the Company&#8217;s supplier finance programs are included in accounts payable in the Consolidated Balance Sheets, and the associated payments are reflected in the cash flows from operating activities section of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows.</p> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric>

GEM and Medifill are included in our&#160;Hygiene,&#160;Health and Consumable Adhesives operating segment.</span></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Restructuring Plans</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">During fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> the Company&#160;approved&#160;restructuring plans (the "Plans")&#160;related to&#160;organizational changes and other actions to optimize operations and integrate acquired businesses. The Plans were implemented in the <em style="font: inherit;">second</em> quarter of fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em> and were completed as of <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29,&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">2025.</em> Remaining cash payments will continue into fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em> In implementing the Plans, the Company currently expects to incur pre-tax costs of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142492915" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-EmployeeSeveranceMember_RestructuringPlanAxis-ThePlanRelatedToOrganizationalChangesAndOtherActionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedCostExpectedCost1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">85,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142492916" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-OtherRestructuringMember_RestructuringPlanAxis-ThePlanRelatedToOrganizationalChangesAndOtherActionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedCostExpectedCost1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">90,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for severance and related employee costs globally, and other restructuring costs related to the streamlining of processes and the payment of anticipated income taxes in certain jurisdictions related to the Plans.</p>

   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><i>Other Restructuring</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">During the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> the Company approved other restructuring actions related to global footprint optimization. The other restructuring actions began to be implemented in the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> and are currently expected to be completed during fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2028.</em> Restructuring costs are expected to be incurred over the next several fiscal quarters as the measures are implemented with the majority of the charges recognized and cash payments occurring in fiscal <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;">2027.</em> In implementing the other restructuring actions, the Company currently expects to incur pre-tax costs of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c142492924" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-EmployeeSeveranceMember_RestructuringPlanAxis-OtherRestructuringActionsRelatedToGlobalFootprintOptimizationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedCostExpectedCost1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">10,200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142492925" contextRef="i_2026-02-28_RestructuringCostAndReserveAxis-OtherRestructuringMember_RestructuringPlanAxis-OtherRestructuringActionsRelatedToGlobalFootprintOptimizationMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:RestructuringAndRelatedCostExpectedCost1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">12,200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;for severance and related employee costs globally, and other restructuring costs related to optimizing the Company&#8217;s footprint and the payment of anticipated income taxes in certain jurisdictions related to the actions.</p>

   <p style="margin: 0; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Basic earnings per share is calculated by dividing net income attributable to H.B. Fuller by the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the applicable period. Diluted earnings per share is based upon the weighted-average number of common and common equivalent shares outstanding during the applicable period. The difference between basic and diluted earnings per share is attributable to share-based compensation awards. We use the treasury stock method to calculate the effect of outstanding shares, which computes total employee proceeds as the sum of (a) the amount the employee must pay upon exercise of the award and (b) the amount of unearned share-based compensation costs attributed to future services. Share-based compensation awards for which total employee proceeds exceed the average market price over the applicable period have an antidilutive effect on earnings per share, and accordingly, are excluded from the calculation of diluted earnings per share.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Share-based compensation awards of&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c142493402" contextRef="d_2025-11-30_2026-02-28" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:AntidilutiveSecuritiesExcludedFromComputationOfEarningsPerShareAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,908,350</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction id="c142493403" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-03-01" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:AntidilutiveSecuritiesExcludedFromComputationOfEarningsPerShareAmount" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">2,140,479</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares for the <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> March 1, 2025</em>, respectively, were excluded from diluted earnings per share calculations because they were antidilutive.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>
  <div>
    &#160;
  </div>
  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-11-30_2026-02-28" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3146149" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">10:</em> Financial Instruments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Overview</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As a result of being a global enterprise,&#160;foreign currency exchange rates and fluctuations in those rates <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>affect the Company's net investment in foreign subsidiaries&#160;and our earnings, cash flows and financial position are exposed to foreign currency risk from foreign currency denominated receivables and payables.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We use foreign currency forward contracts, cross-currency swaps,&#160;interest rate swaps and net investment hedges to manage risks associated with foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> hold derivative financial instruments of a speculative nature or for trading purposes. We record derivatives as assets and liabilities on the balance sheet at fair value. Changes in fair value are recognized immediately in earnings unless the derivative qualifies and is designated as a hedge. Cash flows from derivatives are classified in the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows in the same category as the cash flows from the items subject to designated hedge or undesignated (economic) hedge relationships. We evaluate hedge effectiveness at inception and on an ongoing basis. If a derivative is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer expected to be effective, hedge accounting is discontinued. Hedge ineffectiveness, if any, is recorded in earnings.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We are exposed to credit risk in the event of nonperformance of counterparties for foreign currency forward exchange contracts and interest rate swap agreements. We select investment-grade multinational banks and financial institutions as counterparties for derivative transactions and monitor the credit quality of each of these banks on a periodic basis as warranted. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> anticipate nonperformance by any of these counterparties, and valuation allowances, if any, are de minimis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

This is related to the portion excluded from the assessment of hedge effectiveness for the net investment hedges<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> in the amount of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142493465" contextRef="d_2025-11-30_2026-02-28_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis-CrossCurrencyInterestRateContractMember_DerivativeInstrumentsGainLossByHedgingRelationshipAxis-NetInvestmentHedgingMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GainLossFromComponentsExcludedFromAssessmentOfCashFlowHedgeEffectivenessNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">706</ix:nonFraction>.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Derivatives <em style="font: inherit;">Not</em> Designated as Hedging Instruments</span></i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We use&#160;foreign currency forward contracts to offset our&#160;exposure to the change in value of certain foreign currency denominated assets and liabilities held at foreign subsidiaries that are remeasured at the end of each period. Although the contracts are effective economic hedges, they are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as accounting hedges. Foreign currency forward contracts are recorded as assets and liabilities on the balance sheet at fair value. Changes in the value of these derivatives are recognized immediately in earnings, thereby offsetting the current earnings effect of the related foreign currency denominated assets and liabilities. See Note <em style="font: inherit;">11</em>&#160;for the fair value amounts of these derivative instruments.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>, we had forward foreign currency contracts maturing<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> between <em style="font: inherit;"> March 2, 2026&#160;</em>a</span>nd <em style="font: inherit;"> July 8, 2026. </em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">The ma</span>rk-to-market effect associated with these contracts was largely offset by the underlying transaction gains and losses resulting from the foreign currency exposures for which these contracts relate.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The amounts of pre<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">tax gains&#160;</span>recognized in other income, net related to derivative instruments <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging instruments for the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">three</em> months ended <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> March 1, 2025</em> wer<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">e $<ix:nonFraction id="c142493471" contextRef="d_2025-11-30_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsNotDesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentsGainLossNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2,920</ix:nonFraction> a</span>nd $<ix:nonFraction id="c142493472" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-03-01" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsNotDesignatedAsHedgingInstrumentsGainLossNet" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">40</ix:nonFraction>,&#160;respectively.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Concentrations of credit risk with respect to trade accounts receivable are limited due to the large number of entities in the customer base and their dispersion across many different industries and countries. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em>, there were <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> significant concentrations of credit risk.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-11-30_2026-02-28" name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="c3146151" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">11:</em> Fair Value Measurements </b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Overview</i></p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Estimates of fair value for financial assets and liabilities are based on the framework established in the accounting guidance for fair value measurements. The framework defines fair value, provides guidance for measuring fair value and requires certain disclosures. The framework discusses valuation techniques, such as the market approach (comparable market prices), the income approach (present value of future income or cash flow) and the cost approach (cost to replace the service capacity of an asset or replacement cost). The framework utilizes a fair value hierarchy that prioritizes the inputs to valuation techniques used to measure fair value into <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> broad levels. The following is a brief description of those <em style="font: inherit;">three</em> levels:</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; text-indent: 0px;">
    <tbody>
     <tr style="vertical-align: top;">
      <td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td>
      <td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#9679;</p> </td>
      <td> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1:</em> Observable inputs such as quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.</p> </td>
     </tr>

     <tr style="vertical-align: top;">
      <td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td>
      <td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#9679;</p> </td>
      <td> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2:</em> Inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly or indirectly. These include quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets and quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities in markets that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> active.</p> </td>
     </tr>

     <tr style="vertical-align: top;">
      <td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td>
      <td style="width: 18pt;"> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#9679;</p> </td>
      <td> <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3:</em> Unobservable inputs that reflect management&#8217;s assumptions, and include situations where there is little, if any, market activity for the asset or liability.</p> </td>
     </tr>

    </tbody>
   </table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>

       <em style="font: inherit;">13</em>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><i>Balances Measured at Fair Value on a Nonrecurring Basis</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We measure certain assets and liabilities at fair value on a nonrecurring basis. These assets include&#160;intangible assets acquired&#160;in an acquisition. The identified intangible assets of customer relationships, technology and tradenames acquired in connection with our acquisitions were measured using unobservable (Level&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) inputs. The fair value of the intangible assets was calculated using either the income or cost approach. Significant inputs include estimated revenue growth rates, gross margins, operating expenses, attrition rate, royalty rate and discount rate.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">See Note&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>&#160;for further discussion regarding our acquisitions.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><i>Balances Disclosed at Fair Value</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Long-term debt had an estimated fair value <span style="background-color:#ffffff;">of&#160;</span>$<ix:nonFraction id="c142493493" contextRef="i_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtFairValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,115,526</ix:nonFraction><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;a</span>nd&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142493494" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LongTermDebtFairValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,041,062</ix:nonFraction> as of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em>, respectively. The fair value of long-term debt is based on quoted market prices for the same or similar issues or on the current rates offered for debt of similar maturities. The estimated fair value of these long-term obligations is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of the amount that would be realized in a current market exchange.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">12:</em> Commitments and Contingencies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Environmental Matters</i>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We are involved in environmental investigations, clean-up activities and administrative proceedings related to environmental compliance matters at former and current operating facilities.&#160;&#160; We have also been identified as a potentially responsible party (&#8220;PRP&#8221;) under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (&#8220;CERCLA&#8221;) and/or similar state laws that impose liability for costs relating to the clean-up of contamination resulting from past spills, disposal or other release of hazardous substances associated with landfills and/or hazardous waste sites. As a PRP, we <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required to pay a share of the costs of investigation and clean-up of these sites. We are subject to similar laws in some of the countries where current and former facilities are located. Our environmental, health and safety department monitors compliance with applicable laws on a global basis. To the extent we can reasonably estimate the amount of our probable liabilities for environmental matters, we establish an undiscounted financial provision.&#160;We recorded liabilities of&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142493590" contextRef="i_2026-02-28" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingencies" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,666</ix:nonFraction> and&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142493591" contextRef="i_2025-11-29" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AccrualForEnvironmentalLossContingencies" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">2,625</ix:nonFraction>&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026</em> and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025</em>, respectively, for probable and reasonably estimable environmental remediation costs.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">While uncertainties exist with respect to the amounts and timing of the ultimate environmental liabilities, based on currently available information, we have concluded that these matters, individually or in the aggregate, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition or cash flow.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Other Legal Proceedings</i>&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">From time to time and in the ordinary course of business, we are a party to, or a target of, lawsuits, claims, investigations and proceedings, including product liability, personal injury, contract, patent and intellectual property, environmental, health and safety, tax and employment matters. While we are unable to predict the outcome of these matters, we have concluded, based upon currently available information, that the ultimate resolution of any pending matter, individually or in the aggregate, including the asbestos litigation described in the following paragraphs, will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition or cash flow.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We have been named as a defendant in lawsuits in which plaintiffs have alleged injury due to products containing asbestos manufactured more than <em style="font: inherit;">35</em> years ago. The plaintiffs generally bring these lawsuits against multiple defendants and seek damages (both actual and punitive) in very large amounts. In many cases, plaintiffs are unable to demonstrate that they have suffered any compensable injuries or that the injuries suffered were the result of exposure to products manufactured by us. We are typically dismissed as a defendant in such cases without payment. If the plaintiff presents evidence indicating that compensable injury occurred as a result of exposure to our products, the case is generally settled for an amount that reflects the seriousness of the injury, the length, intensity and character of exposure to products containing asbestos, the number and solvency of other defendants in the case, and the jurisdiction in which the case has been brought.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">A significant portion of the defense costs and settlements in asbestos-related litigation is paid by <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties, including indemnification pursuant to the provisions of a <em style="font: inherit;">1976</em> agreement under which we acquired a business from a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. Currently, this <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party is defending and paying settlement amounts, under a reservation of rights, in most of the asbestos cases tendered to the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In addition to the indemnification arrangements with <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties, we have insurance policies that generally provide coverage for asbestos liabilities, including defense costs.&#160;Historically, insurers have paid a significant portion of our defense costs and settlements in asbestos-related litigation. However, certain of our insurers are insolvent.&#160;We have entered into cost-sharing agreements with our insurers that provide for the allocation of defense costs and settlements and judgments in asbestos-related lawsuits.&#160;These agreements require, among other things, that we fund a share of&#160;settlements and judgments allocable to years in which the responsible insurer is insolvent.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> believe that it would be meaningful to disclose the aggregate number of asbestos-related lawsuits filed against us because relatively few of these lawsuits are known to involve exposure to asbestos-containing products that we manufactured. Rather, we believe it is more meaningful to disclose the number of lawsuits that are settled and result in a payment to the plaintiff. To the extent we can reasonably estimate the amount of our probable liabilities for pending asbestos-related claims, we establish a financial provision and a corresponding receivable for insurance recoveries.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> February 2024,&#160;</em>the named plaintiffs in&#160;<i>Rouse et al. v. H.B. Fuller Company et al.</i>&#160;filed a&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">third</em>&#160;amended complaint in their lawsuit against the Company and&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;of its subsidiaries, which was initiated in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> September 2022.&#160;</em>The suit is pending in the federal District of Minnesota and seeks damages arising from property damage attributed to alleged defects in grout sold by the Company&#8217;s divested North America Flooring business. As previously disclosed, the Company and the plaintiffs agreed in principle to settle this matter for up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c142493606" contextRef="d_2024-02-01_2024-02-28_LitigationCaseAxis-RouseEtAlVHbFullerMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LitigationSettlementAmountAwardedToOtherParty" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">75.0</ix:nonFraction> million. Under the proposed settlement, in lieu of funding the maximum settlement amount, the Company&#8217;s payment obligations will be limited to validly submitted claims, settlement administration costs, service awards, and plaintiffs&#8217; attorneys&#8217; fees and expenses.<b> </b>The terms of a definitive settlement agreement will be subject to court approval. In light of these developments, the Company concluded that a loss is probable and reasonably estimable and recorded an accrual in anticipation of the settlement of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142493607" contextRef="d_2024-02-01_2024-02-28_LitigationCaseAxis-RouseEtAlVHbFullerMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LitigationSettlementLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">34.8</ix:nonFraction> million ($<ix:nonFraction id="c142493608" contextRef="d_2024-02-01_2024-02-28_LitigationCaseAxis-RouseEtAlVHbFullerMember" unitRef="USD" name="ful:LitigationSettlementLossAfterTax" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">26.3</ix:nonFraction> million after tax) based on a range of possible outcomes. This accrual is included in other accrued expenses in the Consolidated Balance Sheets as of <em style="font: inherit;"> February 28, 2026 </em>and <em style="font: inherit;"> November 29, 2025. </em>The Company believes that it is entitled to reimbursement from its insurers for a substantial portion of the potential settlement amount as well as legal fees already incurred and paid and is actively pursuing reimbursement from its insurers.</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">
     Based on currently available information, we have concluded that the resolution of any pending matter, including asbestos-related litigation, individually or in the aggregate, will
    <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition or cash flow.

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">13:</em> Share Repurchase Program</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> April&#160;</em><em style="font: inherit;">22,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2022,</em> the Board of Directors authorized a&#160;share repurchase program of up to&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c142493631" contextRef="i_2022-04-22_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-The2022ShareRepurchaseProgramMember" unitRef="USD" name="srt:StockRepurchaseProgramAuthorizedAmount1" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-8">300,000</ix:nonFraction> of our outstanding common shares for a period of up to <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142493632">five</span> years.&#160;Under the&#160;program, we are authorized to repurchase shares for cash on the open market, from time to time, in privately negotiated transactions or block transactions, or&#160;through an accelerated repurchase agreement. The timing of such repurchases is dependent on price, market conditions and applicable regulatory&#160;requirements. Upon repurchasing&#160;shares, we reduce&#160;our common stock for the par value of the shares with the excess being applied against additional&#160;paid-in capital.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><br/> During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>, we did <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142493635">not</span> repurchase&#160;shares under this program.&#160;During the&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, we repurchased shares under this program&#160;with an&#160;aggregate value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c142493638" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-03-01_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-The2022ShareRepurchaseProgramMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">41,153</ix:nonFraction><span style="background-color:#ffffff">.</span> Of this amount, $<ix:nonFraction id="c142493639" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-03-01_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-The2022ShareRepurchaseProgramMember_StatementEquityComponentsAxis-CommonStockMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">678</ix:nonFraction>&#160;reduced common stock and $<ix:nonFraction id="c142493640" contextRef="d_2024-12-01_2025-03-01_ShareRepurchaseProgramAxis-The2022ShareRepurchaseProgramMember_StatementEquityComponentsAxis-AdditionalPaidInCapitalMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">40,475</ix:nonFraction>&#160;reduced additional paid-in capital.&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">14:</em> Segments</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Our <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c142493642">three</span> reportable&#160;operating segments consist&#160;of Hygiene, Health and Consumable Adhesives, Engineering Adhesives&#160;and Building Adhesive Solutions.&#160;We are required to report segment information in the same way that we internally organize our business for assessing performance and making decisions regarding allocation of resources.&#160;Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA of each of our segments are regularly reviewed by our chief executive officer, who acts as our chief operating decision maker, to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segments and assess their performance. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization&#160;and foreign currency gain/loss, adjusted for other items within a relevant period which are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> reflective of the segment&#8217;s operating performance in the period.&#160;Corporate expenses, other than those included in Corporate Unallocated, are allocated to each operating segment.&#160;Consistent with our internal management reporting, Corporate Unallocated includes and Adjusted EBITDA excludes amounts related to business acquisition and integration costs, organizational restructuring charges and project costs associated with our implementation of a global Enterprise Resource Planning ("ERP") system that we refer to as Project ONE. Corporate assets are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> allocated to the operating segments. Inter-segment revenues are recorded at cost plus a markup for administrative costs. See below for a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to net income attributable H.B. Fuller as reflected in the audited consolidated statement of income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The business components within each operating segment are managed to maximize the results of the overall operating segment rather than the results of any individual business component of the operating segment. Results of individual components of each operating segment are subject to numerous allocations of segment-wide costs that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have been focused on that particular component for a particular reporting period. The costs for these allocated resources are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> tracked on a &#8220;where-used&#8221; basis as financial performance is assessed at the total operating segment level.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b><a id="mda" title="mda" href="#"></a>Item 2. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Overview</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (&#8220;MD&amp;A&#8221;) should be read in conjunction with the MD&amp;A included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended November 29, 2025, for important background information related to our business.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Net revenue in the&#160;first quarter of&#160;2026&#160;decreased 2.3&#160;percent from the first quarter of 2025. The decrease&#160;was due to&#160;a&#160;7.2&#160;percent decrease due to sales volume, partially offset by&#160;a&#160;3.6&#160;percent increase due to positive&#160;currency effects, a&#160;0.7&#160;percent increase due to&#160;acquisitions&#160;and a&#160;0.6&#160;percent increase due to pricing compared to the&#160;first quarter of 2025.&#160;The positive&#160;currency effect&#160;was&#160;primarily driven<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> by a stronger Euro,&#160;Chinese renminbi,&#160;British pound, Brazilian real, Mexican peso and Australian dollar partially offset by a weaker T</span><span style="color:#000000"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">urkish lira</span></span><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;compared to the U.S. dollar. Gross profit margin increased </span>180<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;basis points primarily&#160;</span>due to&#160;higher product pricing, lower raw material&#160;costs, the impact of acquisitions and restructuring actions.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">Net income attributable to H.B. Fuller in the </span>first<span style="color:#000000;"> quarter of&#160;</span>2026<span style="color:#000000;"> was </span>$21.0<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;million compared to </span>$13.2<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;million in the </span>first<span style="color:#000000;"> quarter of </span>2025<span style="color:#000000;">. Diluted earnings per share for the </span>first<span style="color:#000000;"> quarter of&#160;</span>2026<span style="color:#000000;"> was </span>$0.38<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;per share compared to </span>$0.24<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;per share for the </span>first<span style="color:#000000;"> quarter of </span>2025<span style="color:#000000;">.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="color:#000000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Adjusted EBITDA in the first</span></span><span style="color:#ff0000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;</span></span>three<span style="color:#ff0000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;</span></span><span style="color:#000000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">months of</span></span><span style="color:#ff0000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;</span></span>2026 <span style="color:#000000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">increased&#160;</span>3.8<span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> percent from&#160;the&#160;first</span></span> three <span style="color:#000000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">months of</span></span> 2025<span style="color:#000000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">, primarily driven by higher net income and depreciation and amortization expense.&#160;</span></span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Restructuring Plans</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">During fiscal year 2023, the Company&#160;approved&#160;restructuring plans (the &#8220;Plans&#8221;) related to&#160;organizational changes and other actions to optimize operations and integrate acquired businesses. In implementing the Plans, the Company currently expects to incur costs of approximately $85.0 million to $90.0 million ($58.0&#160;million to $61.4&#160;million after tax), which include&#160;(i) cash expenditures of approximately $51.0&#160;million to $52.0&#160;million ($34.8&#160;million to $35.5&#160;million after tax) for severance and related employee costs globally and (ii) other restructuring costs related to the streamlining of processes and the payment of anticipated income taxes in certain jurisdictions related to the Plans. We have incurred costs of $83.2 million under the&#160;Plans as of </span>February 28, 2026<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">. Remaining cash payments will continue into fiscal year 2026.</span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">During the first quarter of 2026, the Company approved other restructuring actions related to global footprint optimization. In implementing the other restructuring actions, the Company currently expects to incur costs of approximately $10.2&#160;million to $12.2&#160;million ($7.5&#160;million to $9.0&#160;million after tax), which include (i) cash expenditures of approximately $5.8&#160;million to $6.8&#160;million ($4.3&#160;million to $5.0&#160;million after tax) for severance and related employee costs globally and (ii) other restructuring costs related to optimizing the Company&#8217;s footprint and the payment of anticipated income taxes in certain jurisdictions related to the other restructuring actions. We have incurred costs of $4.8 million under the other restructuring actions as of February 28, 2026. The other restructuring actions began to be implemented in the first quarter of 2026 and are currently expected to be completed during fiscal year 2028. Restructuring costs are expected to be incurred over the next several fiscal quarters as the measures are implemented with the majority of the charges recognized and cash payments occurring in fiscal 2026 and 2027.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Adjusted EBITDA for H.B. Adjusted EBITDA as a percentage of net revenue increased&#160;90 basis points in the </span>first<span style="color:#000000"> quarter of&#160;</span>2026 <span style="color:#000000">compared to</span><span style="color:#000000">&#160;</span>first<span style="color:#000000"> quarter of 2025</span>&#160;due to higher net income and depreciation and amortization expense. For a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to net income attributable to H.B. Fuller as reflected in the unaudited consolidated statement of income see "Non-GAAP Measures" below.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><span style="color:#000000;"><b>Operating Segment Results</b></span></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">Our three reportable&#160;operating segments consist&#160;of Hygiene, Health and Consumable Adhesives, Engineering Adhesives&#160;and Building Adhesive Solutions.&#160;</span>We are required to report segment information in the same way that we internally organize our business for assessing performance and making decisions regarding allocation of resources.&#160;Revenue and Adjusted EBITDA of each of our segments are regularly reviewed by our chief executive officer, who acts as our chief operating decision maker, to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segments and assess their performance. Adjusted EBITDA is defined as net income before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization and foreign currency gain/loss, adjusted for other items within a relevant period which are not reflective of the segment&#8217;s operating performance in the period.&#160;Corporate expenses, other than those included in Corporate Unallocated, are allocated to each operating segment.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The tables below provide certain information regarding the net revenue,&#160;Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin of each of our operating segments. Adjusted EBITDA margin is defined as Adjusted EBITDA divided by net revenue for each operating segment. Corporate Unallocated amounts include&#160;business acquisition and integration costs, organizational restructuring charges and project costs associated with implementing a global Enterprise Resource Planning (&#8220;ERP&#8221;) system that we refer to as Project ONE.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><span style="color:#000000;">Net revenue decreased </span>5.9<span style="color:#000000;">&#160;percent in the </span>first<span style="color:#000000;"> quarter of&#160;</span>2026<span style="color:#000000;"> compared to the </span>first<span style="color:#000000;"> quarter of </span>2025<span style="color:#000000;">.&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;">Organic revenue growth decreased due to decrease in sales volume&#160;and&#160;<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">product pricing. The&#160;</span></span>0.8<span style="color:#000000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> percent increase in net revenue from M&amp;A was due to the acquisitions of GEM&#160;and Medifill&#160;in the first quarter of 2025.&#160;The positive currency effect was due to&#160;a stronger Euro, Brazilian real, Mexican peso and Chinese renminbi, partially offset by a weaker Turkish lira&#160;compared&#160;to the U.S. dollar. </span></span>Segment adjusted EBITDA increased 2.3&#160;percent&#160;<span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);"><span style="color: #000000; ">in&#160;the first quarter of&#160;2026 compared to the first quarter of 2025</span>.&#160;</span><span style="color:#000000;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">Segment adjusted&#160;EBITDA margin&#160;increased 120 basis points primarily due to lower revenue, lower raw materials cost&#160;and the impact of acquisitions.</span></span></p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b>Financial Condition, Liquidity and Capital Resources</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Total cash and cash equivalents as of February 28, 2026 were $107.9&#160;million compared to&#160;$107.2&#160;million as of November 29, 2025 and&#160;$105.7 million as of March 1, 2025. The majority of the $107.9&#160;million in cash and cash equivalents as of February 28, 2026 was held outside the United States. Total long and short-term debt was $2,076.1&#160;million as of February 28, 2026, $2,016.9&#160;million as of November 29, 2025 and $2,180.0&#160;million as of March 1, 2025. The total debt to total capital ratio as measured by total debt divided by total debt plus total stockholders&#8217; equity&#160;was&#160;50.1 percent as of February 28, 2026 as compared to&#160;50.2 percent as of November 29, 2025 and&#160;55.1 percent as of March 1, 2025.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We believe that cash flows from operating activities will be adequate to meet our short-term and long-term liquidity and capital expenditure needs.&#160;In addition, we believe we have the ability to obtain both short-term and long-term debt to meet our financing needs for the foreseeable future.&#160;Cash available in the United States has historically been sufficient and we expect it will continue to be sufficient to fund U.S. operations, U.S. capital spending and U.S. pension and other postretirement benefit contributions in addition to funding U.S. acquisitions, dividend payments, debt service and share repurchases as needed. For those international earnings considered to be reinvested indefinitely, we currently have no intention to, and plans do not indicate a need to, repatriate these funds for U.S. operations.</p>

As of&#160;February 28, 2026, we were in compliance with all covenants of our credit agreement contractual obligations as shown in the following table:</p>

For Secured Total Indebtedness / TTM EBITDA ratio, TTM EBITDA is adjusted for the pro forma results from Material Acquisitions and Material Divestitures, both as defined in the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, as if the acquisition or divestiture occurred at the beginning of the calculation period.&#160;The full definition is set forth in the Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement filed as an exhibit to the Company's 8-K filing&#160;dated February 21, 2023.</td>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:25.2pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-7.2pt;"><span style="font-size:9pt"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">3 </sup></span>Total inventory multiplied by 91 (13 weeks) and divided by cost of sales (excluding delivery costs) for the quarter.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:25.2pt;margin-right:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-7.2pt;"><span style="font-size:9pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">5</sup></span> Year-to-date net cash provided by operating activities, less purchased property, plant and equipment.&#160;See "Non GAAP Measures" for reconciliation of net cash provided by operating activities to free cash flow.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 9pt; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 25.2pt; text-align: justify; text-indent: -7.2pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">6</sup> <span style="font-size:10pt;">Total debt divided by (total debt plus total stockholders&#8217; equity).</span></p>
  <div style="font-size: 10px;">
    &#160;
  </div>
  <p style="margin: 0px; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Free cash flow, a non-GAAP financial measure, is defined as net cash provided by operating activities less purchased property, plant and equipment. Free cash flow is an integral financial measure used by the Company to assess its ability to generate cash in excess of its operating needs, therefore, the Company believes this financial measure provides useful information to investors. For a reconciliation of net cash provided by operating activities to free cash flow see &#8220;Non-GAAP Measures&#8221; below.</p>
  <p style="margin: 0; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;"><b>Non-GAAP Measures</b>&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We use both GAAP and non-GAAP financial measures for operational and financial decision making, and to assess Company and segment business performance. Our non-GAAP measures include Adjusted EBITDA&#160;and Free Cash Flow. Our calculation of these non-GAAP measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies due to potential differences between companies in the method of calculation. As a result, the use of these non-GAAP measures has limitations and should not be considered superior to, in isolation from, or as a substitute for, related U.S. GAAP measures.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">These non-GAAP measures allow management and investors to view operating trends, perform analytical comparisons and benchmark performance between periods and among geographic regions to understand operating performance without regard to items we do not consider a component of our core operating performance. Furthermore, these non-GAAP measures allow investors the opportunity to measure and monitor our performance against our externally communicated targets and evaluate the investment decisions being made by management to improve Adjusted EBITDA. Management uses these measures in its financial, investment and operational decision-making processes, for internal reporting and as part of its forecasting and budgeting processes. Further, our Board of Directors uses certain of these and other measures as key metrics to determine management performance under our performance-based compensation plans. For these reasons, we believe these non-GAAP measures are useful for our investors.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Adjusted EBITDA is presented net of noncontrolling interests and is used by management and can be used by investors to review our consolidated operating results because it excludes depreciation, amortization, interest income, interest expense and income taxes as well as certain additional adjustments that are not considered part of our core operations. Examples of adjustments to EBITDA include, but are not limited to, costs for acquisition projects, organizational realignment, Project One, business divestitures, discrete taxes, and the income tax effect on these adjustments.&#160; For Adjusted EBITDA, once we have made an adjustment in the current period for an item, we will also adjust the related non-GAAP measure in future periods in which there is an impact from the item. The following table reflects the manner in which Adjusted EBITDA is determined and provides a reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to Net income attributable to H.B. Fuller, the most directly comparable financial measure calculated and reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP.</p>

Free cash flow is an integral financial measure used by the Company to assess its ability to generate cash in excess of its operating needs, therefore, the Company believes this financial measure provides useful information to investors. The following table reflects the manner in which free cash flow is determined and provides a reconciliation of free cash flow to net cash provided by operating activities, the most directly comparable financial measure calculated and reported in accordance with U.S. GAAP.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><a id="contpro" title="contpro" href="#"></a>Item 4. Controls and Procedures</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Controls and Procedures</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We conducted an evaluation, under the supervision and with the participation of our president and chief executive officer and executive vice president, chief financial officer, of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e) under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Exchange Act)) as of February 28, 2026.&#160;Based on this evaluation, our president and chief executive officer and executive vice president, chief financial officer concluded that, as of February 28, 2026, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">For purposes of Rule 13a-15(e), the term <i>disclosure controls and procedures</i> means controls and other procedures of an issuer that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by the issuer in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act (15 U.S.C. 78a et seq.) is recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#8217;s rules and forms. Disclosure controls and procedures include, without limitation, controls and procedures designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed by an issuer in the reports that it files or submits under the Exchange Act is accumulated and communicated to the issuer&#8217;s management, including its president and chief executive officer and executive vice president, chief financial officer, or persons performing similar functions, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left;"><b><a id="legal" title="legal" href="#"></a>Item 1. Legal Proceedings</b></p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Environmental Matters</i>&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We are&#160;involved in environmental investigations, clean-up activities and administrative proceedings related to environmental compliance matters at former and current operating facilities.&#160;&#160; We have also been&#160;identified as a potentially responsible party (&#8220;PRP&#8221;) under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (CERCLA) and/or similar state laws that impose liability for costs relating to the clean up of contamination resulting from past spills, disposal or other release of hazardous substances associated with landfills and/or hazardous waste sites. As a PRP, we may be required to pay a share of the costs of investigation and clean-up of these sites. We are subject to similar laws in some of the countries where current and former facilities are located. Our environmental, health and safety department monitors compliance with applicable laws on a global basis.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt 7.5pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">To the extent we can reasonably estimate the amount of our probable liabilities for environmental matters, we establish a financial provision.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">While uncertainties exist with respect to the amounts and timing of the ultimate environmental liabilities, based on currently available information, we have concluded that these matters, individually or in the aggregate, will not have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition or cash flow.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:0pt;margin-right:7.5pt;margin-top:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Other Legal Proceedings</i>&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">From time to time and in the ordinary course of business, we are a party to, or a target of, lawsuits, claims, investigations and proceedings, including product liability, personal injury, contract, patent and intellectual property, environmental, health and safety, tax and employment matters. While we are unable to predict the outcome of these matters, we have concluded, based upon currently available information, that the ultimate resolution of any pending matter, individually or in the aggregate, including asbestos-related litigation, will not have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition or cash flow. However, adverse developments and/or periodic settlements could negatively impact the results of operations or cash flows in one or more future periods.</p>
